text: Final lab. A screen flow a rep actually runs, the moment a deal closes — and the one flow type in this course that finally gets to put $Flow.FaultMessage exactly where Lesson 20 first showed it: right on a screen.

Right now, onboarding happens by memory — someone has to remember to create a contact, a task, schedule a kickoff for the bigger deals. A guided wizard turns hopefully remembered into walked through, every time.

Opportunity - Screen - Onboarding Wizard, launched from a Quick Action right on the closed Opportunity. Screen one confirms the account, read-only, then collects the primary contact's name and email, plus one checkbox: does this deal need an implementation project.

A Decision reads that checkbox — Needs Implementation Project — and only the Yes path reaches a second screen to schedule the kickoff call. Standard deals skip straight past it. Same branching pattern from the Decisions lesson, just gating an entire screen instead of one field.

Then two Create Records elements — the primary Contact, and an onboarding Task assigned to the account owner. And here's the payoff: unlike the last two labs, this is a screen flow, so a fault path off Create Primary Contact can show $Flow.FaultMessage directly on a screen — the pattern exactly as Lesson 20 first introduced it, no field workaround needed.

That closes Flow Automation — 31 lessons of elements, data types, testing, bulkification, limits, versioning, orchestration, and three full labs, all of it built from the same handful of elements used honestly. Next up in the Salesforce Administrator path: Business Process Automation, picking up where declarative automation meets the rest of the platform.
